Several major US districts have already drawn hard lines. Los Angeles Unified announced a moratorium on generative AI across all grades in early September 2026.
New York City has placed limits on AI usage in schools through 8th grade. That covers the country’s largest school system for most of its younger students.
Frederick County’s school district went further on October 7, 2026, voting to ban generative AI from pre-K through 12th grade.
Those decisions were made before Google’s announcement. Now each of those districts faces a new question: does a ban on generative AI also mean a ban on Google Search?
Google isn’t only flipping switches. The company plans to pilot a feature called Guided Learning, designed to encourage students to work through problems rather than receive instant answers.
The idea is to make AI behave more like a tutor than an answer key. Instead of spitting out the solution to a math problem, the tool would nudge students toward reasoning it out themselves.

The most immediate impact falls on school administrators, who now carry the decision explicitly. Under the new default, inaction disables AI and search, so districts can’t simply let the status quo ride.
That shifts accountability in a notable way. If AI shows up in a classroom, it’s because a school chose it, not because Google pushed it there by default.

For districts with existing bans, the tradeoff is steeper. Los Angeles Unified, New York City and Frederick County will each need to decide whether their AI restrictions are worth losing Google Search for students, or whether to revisit the scope of those policies.

The no-granular-controls position is likely to be the most debated part of the plan. Schools that are comfortable with traditional search but wary of AI summaries have no middle option under the approach Phillips described.

The broader signal is about how far AI has spread into everyday software. Google’s position is that AI and search are now effectively the same product. For K-12 schools, that framing turns a narrow debate about chatbots into a much larger decision about basic internet access for students.

coreStoryFacts.text: Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post that Search, along with Google's Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook and Gemini in Google Classroom, will be set off by default for K-12 student accounts until school administrators turn them on.

The company said it would share more specifics with schools "in the coming months" ahead of the rollout and that the decision followed conversations with schools, teachers, researchers and policymakers.

(Bloomberg) -- Schools that want their K-12 students to have access to Google Search will soon have to turn it on themselves, and the AI features built into Search will come with it, under changes the Alphabet Inc. company announced Tuesday.
The company also said Guided Learning, a study mode Google first released in its Gemini app, would be extended into Search.
When Google's systems detect a student is looking for certain types of homework help, Search will walk them through a problem one step at a time.
A student who pastes in a physics problem or asks for help with a book report, for example, will get prompts meant to make them work through the concepts instead of skipping to the answer.
The change comes as Google, whose Chromebooks are the most widely used laptops in American classrooms, faces growing resistance to AI from parents and school districts.
Google will pilot Guided Learning within Google Search in select US schools later this month and plans to expand it to other districts after collecting feedback from teachers.
Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on.
The tech giant says the change follows consultations with schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers.
As a result, Google is revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search.

Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” which means that if a school chooses to restrict AI altogether, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”
However, Google Search and its AI features are now inseparable.
Given the dominance of Google’s suite of apps in classrooms and the widespread use of Chromebooks, the decision underscores the company’s influence over the education sector.
Google announced the upcoming change alongside the launch of Guided Learning in schools.
The tool, which was unveiled earlier this year, sort of functions like an AI tutor, as it’s designed to help users build a deep understanding instead of just getting answers.
The launch comes amid concerns that AI chatbots undermine the learning process because they spit out direct answers.

Although teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews in Google Search to conduct research or complete assignments, they likely still want them to be able to have access to the search engine to find sources and other learning materials.

sources.title: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search
passages: Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on.
The tech giant says the change follows consultations with schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers.
As a result, Google is revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search.

Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” which means that if a school chooses to restrict AI altogether, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”
However, Google Search and its AI features are now inseparable.
Given the dominance of Google’s suite of apps in classrooms and the widespread use of Chromebooks, the decision underscores the company’s influence over the education sector.
Google announced the upcoming change alongside the launch of Guided Learning in schools.
The tool, which was unveiled earlier this year, sort of functions like an AI tutor, as it’s designed to help users build a deep understanding instead of just getting answers.
The launch comes amid concerns that AI chatbots undermine the learning process because they spit out direct answers.

Although teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews in Google Search to conduct research or complete assignments, they likely still want them to be able to have access to the search engine to find sources and other learning materials.

passages: Starting early 2027, Gemini and Google Search become opt-in for student accounts, and schools can't keep one without the other
Tue 3 Nov 2026 · 11:32 EST · 4 min read

Google is about to give school administrators a choice that isn’t really much of a choice. Starting early next year, its AI tools will be turned off by default for K-12 student accounts, and schools that keep AI disabled will lose Google Search along with it.
That means a district that wants to keep chatbots out of the classroom may also have to keep the world’s most popular search engine out.

Google announced the policy on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The changes apply to student accounts within Google Workspace for Education, the software suite many US schools rely on for email, documents and classwork.
Beginning in early 2027, access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Google Search will be opt-in. The default setting will be disabled.
School administrators will need to actively turn these tools on if they want students to use them. Doing nothing means students get nothing.
The catch is how tightly Google has woven AI into search itself. Features like AI Overviews and AI Mode now sit inside the core search experience, so Google says it can’t cleanly separate the two.

Google VP Chris Phillips emphasized that integration when explaining the decision. According to the research findings, Phillips indicated there will be no granular controls that let schools switch off AI Overviews alone while keeping standard search running.
Google says it plans to share more detailed implementation information in the coming months.

The move lands in the middle of a broader backlash against generative AI in classrooms. Educators and policymakers have raised concerns about cheating and student privacy as AI tools spread through schools faster than rules could keep up.
Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.
We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.
Several major US districts have already drawn hard lines. Los Angeles Unified announced a moratorium on generative AI across all grades in early September 2026.
New York City has placed limits on AI usage in schools through 8th grade. That covers the country’s largest school system for most of its younger students.
Frederick County’s school district went further on October 7, 2026, voting to ban generative AI from pre-K through 12th grade.
Those decisions were made before Google’s announcement. Now each of those districts faces a new question: does a ban on generative AI also mean a ban on Google Search?
Google isn’t only flipping switches. The company plans to pilot a feature called Guided Learning, designed to encourage students to work through problems rather than receive instant answers.
The idea is to make AI behave more like a tutor than an answer key. Instead of spitting out the solution to a math problem, the tool would nudge students toward reasoning it out themselves.

The most immediate impact falls on school administrators, who now carry the decision explicitly. Under the new default, inaction disables AI and search, so districts can’t simply let the status quo ride.
That shifts accountability in a notable way. If AI shows up in a classroom, it’s because a school chose it, not because Google pushed it there by default.

For districts with existing bans, the tradeoff is steeper. Los Angeles Unified, New York City and Frederick County will each need to decide whether their AI restrictions are worth losing Google Search for students, or whether to revisit the scope of those policies.

The no-granular-controls position is likely to be the most debated part of the plan. Schools that are comfortable with traditional search but wary of AI summaries have no middle option under the approach Phillips described.

The broader signal is about how far AI has spread into everyday software. Google’s position is that AI and search are now effectively the same product. For K-12 schools, that framing turns a narrow debate about chatbots into a much larger decision about basic internet access for students.

sources.title: Binance hack: Users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto heist - BBC
passages: Binance customers withdrew $3.6bn (£2.7bn) of assets from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following what is believed to be the largest hack in history.
The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, which stole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025 .

Funds linked to the Binance hack continue to be laundered, according to Alec Zebrick, senior manager in global services at Chainalysis, which has been working with the firm and governments to get the stolen money back.
Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack
Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion."
Watch: What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack and what to do if you're affected
Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance.
The hack hit Binance's global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform has said it was not affected by the issue.
The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source.

extraction.body: (Nov 2): Binance's customers have withdrawn almost US$5 billion (RM20.3 billion) from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened after a hack that saw US$6.3 billion of crypto stolen from the platform in what could be the largest financial heist in history. Customers have withdrawn a net US$4.72 billion since a suspension was lifted on Sunday morning, a spokesperson said. The exchange froze withdrawals for about 48 hours after the hack, which the FBI said was carried out by North Korea. Binance said the net outflow amounted to about 2.8% of assets on the platform, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up. The outflow compares with about US$7 billion withdrawn from Circle's USDC stablecoin over a week after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023. Binance itself processed net outflows of about US$6 billion over 72 hours following the collapse of FTX in December 2022. "Our top priority right now is to ensure the environment is secure, after which users can withdraw their funds and Binance can resume operations," Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X on Monday. Trading volumes increased across the crypto market as investors grappled with what could be the biggest theft from a financial institution ever. The attack marks a step up in North Korea's crypto thefts. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said North Korea-linked hackers have stolen US$7.4 billion so far in 2026. Binance said it was covering the losses with company funds and had already raised US$6 billion from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches. "It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal," said Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, a digital asset financial service company in Hong Kong. Sun said security concerns were likely to influence how much market makers, institutions and other investors allocate to cryptocurrencies. Binance, which says it has more than 335 million users worldwide and average daily trading volumes of US$95 billion across digital assets and derivatives, also sought to reassure customers. "After an initial spike, withdrawal volumes have declined and are stabilising," Binance said on X. A spokesperson said there had been US$2.7 billion in inflows. Some traders told Reuters they were keeping their accounts. "I would not necessarily withdraw everything from Binance, because centralised exchanges continue to play an important role in liquidity, trading and market access," said Jay Koh, vice-president of the Asia Web3 AI Association, a blockchain advocacy group based in Singapore. Ryan Tan, a Binance user, said that he was in no hurry to withdraw his funds from the platform, as he had already kept his account fairly light since the collapse of another crypto exchange, FTX, four years ago. "After the FTX collapse, I decided to hold everything on my wallet instead of leaving them on exchanges," said the 39-year-old. After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin prices recovered through the weekend to trade around US$78,000 on Monday, while ether also rebounded from a two-month low. Stablecoin market capitalisations, often viewed as a gauge of money moving into and out of crypto markets, have fallen since Friday, suggesting some investors have shifted funds into cash or traditional assets. Binance said withdrawals had resumed for bitcoin on the bitcoin network and for ether and some dollar stablecoins on the Ethereum network, though its website still showed withdrawals remained partially suspended for most cryptocurrencies. It restored US dollar cash as a withdrawal option on Monday. The Binance theft is the largest of a string of crypto thefts blamed on North Korea. The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programmes. Analysts said the scale and prominence of the attack could curb institutional appetite for cryptocurrencies, which many investors had hoped would support prices. Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of US$643 million on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than US$1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at US blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs. "A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said. About half of the stolen funds were held in stablecoins and have been frozen by issuers including Circle, which said on Monday it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC. Jonathan Benton, founder and chief executive at crypto asset recovery firm iSanctuary, said the technology exists to trace stolen funds, but the challenge is turning that intelligence into rapid, coordinated action before those assets disappear. "The future of crypto won't be decided by how much money enters the market, but by how safe that money is once it's there," said Benton, former head of the international corruption unit of the UK's National Crime Agency. extraction.body: (Nov 2): Binance's customers have withdrawn almost US$5 billion (RM20.3 billion) from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened after a hack that saw US$6.3 billion of crypto stolen from the platform in what could be the largest financial heist in history. Customers have withdrawn a net US$4.72 billion since a suspension was lifted on Sunday morning, a spokesperson said. The exchange froze withdrawals for about 48 hours after the hack, which the FBI said was carried out by North Korea. Binance said the net outflow amounted to about 2.8% of assets on the platform, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up. The outflow compares with about US$7 billion withdrawn from Circle's USDC stablecoin over a week after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023. Binance itself processed net outflows of about US$6 billion over 72 hours following the collapse of FTX in December 2022. "Our top priority right now is to ensure the environment is secure, after which users can withdraw their funds and Binance can resume operations," Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X on Monday. Trading volumes increased across the crypto market as investors grappled with what could be the biggest theft from a financial institution ever. The attack marks a step up in North Korea's crypto thefts. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said North Korea-linked hackers have stolen US$7.4 billion so far in 2026. Binance said it was covering the losses with company funds and had already raised US$6 billion from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches. "It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal," said Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, a digital asset financial service company in Hong Kong. Sun said security concerns were likely to influence how much market makers, institutions and other investors allocate to cryptocurrencies. Binance, which says it has more than 335 million users worldwide and average daily trading volumes of US$95 billion across digital assets and derivatives, also sought to reassure customers. "After an initial spike, withdrawal volumes have declined and are stabilising," Binance said on X. A spokesperson said there had been US$2.7 billion in inflows. Some traders told Reuters they were keeping their accounts. "I would not necessarily withdraw everything from Binance, because centralised exchanges continue to play an important role in liquidity, trading and market access," said Jay Koh, vice-president of the Asia Web3 AI Association, a blockchain advocacy group based in Singapore. Ryan Tan, a Binance user, said that he was in no hurry to withdraw his funds from the platform, as he had already kept his account fairly light since the collapse of another crypto exchange, FTX, four years ago. "After the FTX collapse, I decided to hold everything on my wallet instead of leaving them on exchanges," said the 39-year-old. After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin prices recovered through the weekend to trade around US$78,000 on Monday, while ether also rebounded from a two-month low. Stablecoin market capitalisations, often viewed as a gauge of money moving into and out of crypto markets, have fallen since Friday, suggesting some investors have shifted funds into cash or traditional assets. Binance said withdrawals had resumed for bitcoin on the bitcoin network and for ether and some dollar stablecoins on the Ethereum network, though its website still showed withdrawals remained partially suspended for most cryptocurrencies. It restored US dollar cash as a withdrawal option on Monday. The Binance theft is the largest of a string of crypto thefts blamed on North Korea. The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programmes. Analysts said the scale and prominence of the attack could curb institutional appetite for cryptocurrencies, which many investors had hoped would support prices. Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of US$643 million on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than US$1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at US blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs. "A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said. About half of the stolen funds were held in stablecoins and have been frozen by issuers including Circle, which said on Monday it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC. Jonathan Benton, founder and chief executive at crypto asset recovery firm iSanctuary, said the technology exists to trace stolen funds, but the challenge is turning that intelligence into rapid, coordinated action before those assets disappear. "The future of crypto won't be decided by how much money enters the market, but by how safe that money is once it's there," said Benton, former head of the international corruption unit of the UK's National Crime Agency. After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin prices recovered through the weekend to trade around US$78,000 on Monday, while ether also rebounded from a two-month low.

Stablecoin market capitalisations, often viewed as a gauge of money moving into and out of crypto markets, have fallen since Friday, suggesting some investors have shifted funds into cash or traditional assets.

Binance said withdrawals had resumed for bitcoin on the bitcoin network and for ether and some dollar stablecoins on the Ethereum network, though its website still showed withdrawals remained partially suspended for most cryptocurrencies.
It restored US dollar cash as a withdrawal option on Monday.
The Binance theft is the largest of a string of crypto thefts blamed on North Korea.

The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programmes.
Analysts said the scale and prominence of the attack could curb institutional appetite for cryptocurrencies, which many investors had hoped would support prices.

Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of US$643 million on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than US$1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at US blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs.
"A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said.
About half of the stolen funds were held in stablecoins and have been frozen by issuers including Circle, which said on Monday it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC.

Jonathan Benton, founder and chief executive at crypto asset recovery firm iSanctuary, said the technology exists to trace stolen funds, but the challenge is turning that intelligence into rapid, coordinated action before those assets disappear.

"The future of crypto won't be decided by how much money enters the market, but by how safe that money is once it's there," said Benton, former head of the international corruption unit of the UK's National Crime Agency.

extraction.body: Apple will soon start asking developers to provide more details about their apps to enforce new App Store age rating requirements for dating and location-sharing features. The upcoming content descriptors announced on Monday will require developers to declare if their apps allow users to share their real-world location with others, or include features that enable dating, relationship, or sexual behaviour between real people or virtual companions. Apps that include dating and relationships features will receive a minimum age rating of 18 while those with location sharing will see an impact to their minimum age rating in some regions, depending on local regulations. These updates will be included in the App Store Connect age rating questionnaire starting November 16th, and all apps will be required to complete the new declarations by January 12th, 2027. Apple already has an 18-plus rating category for the App Store, but this has largely applied to apps that feature gambling; violence; references to drugs, alcohol, or tobacco; and nudity or sexual content. Most dating platforms are also adult-only, but Apple extending its ratings is an effort to prevent minors from slipping through the cracks. These expanding restrictions also aim to keep them away from both AI chatbots that support sexual or romantic interactions, and virtual “girlfriend / boyfriend” simulators that could pose mental health risks.

sources.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
passages: Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.
While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating.
Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said.
As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally .
Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters.
In addition to “dating and relationships,” apps will also need to indicate if they are sharing the real-world locations of a user with another person or group as part of their functionality.

The new rules follow other changes the company has made to better protect minors, which include the rollout of its age assurance technology globally and more parental controls and child safety features . Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said. It’s perhaps more interesting how this rule could impact AI companion apps, or those where such functionality is one of many features. Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters. xAI last year also launched 3D animated AI companions that allowed users to unlock NSFW capabilities . As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally . In addition to “dating and relationships,” apps will also need to indicate if they are sharing the real-world locations of a user with another person or group as part of their functionality. Any app doing so raises obvious privacy concerns, especially if the user wasn’t aware that their location was being shared. The company noted that in Brazil, apps that provide location-sharing features for families can request an official rating from the government’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública), instead of being required to list them with the A16 rating, as the local law requires.

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple will soon start asking developers to provide more details about their apps to enforce new App Store age rating requirements for dating and location-sharing features.

Apple already has an 18-plus rating category for the App Store, but this has largely applied to apps that feature gambling; violence; references to drugs, alcohol, or tobacco; and nudity or sexual content.
Most dating platforms are also adult-only, but Apple extending its ratings is an effort to prevent minors from slipping through the cracks.

Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.
While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating.
Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said.
As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally .
Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters.
In addition to “dating and relationships,” apps will also need to indicate if they are sharing the real-world locations of a user with another person or group as part of their functionality.
Apple requires minimum 18+ rating for dating/romantic and AI companion apps starting November 16, 2026.
Developers must disclose location-sharing features in App Store Connect with new descriptors.

TechCrunch frames the change as a policy that will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating, and it links the update to Apple’s broader effort to better protect minors.
Apple Makes App Store Dating Apps and AI Companions 18+ Only

Apple’s rules also state that apps with the dating descriptor will be hidden from users under 18 on devices where a parent or guardian has turned on content restrictions, and younger users who can still see the app must prove they are adults before they can buy or download it.
Apple will require that dating apps be for users 18 and older

The descriptor keys on features, not on what kind of app it is. A general chatbot with one romantic persona among many could end up rated 18+ as a whole app.

That matters because virtual girlfriend and boyfriend simulators have drawn warnings about mental health risks for younger users. A feature-level rating lets Apple catch those products even when they sit inside a broader assistant. That leaves fewer cracks for minors to slip through, even on apps that never market themselves as companions.

Chatbot makers have mostly set these limits through their own policies, such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT teen safety rules . Apple now moves part of that call onto the store listing. The rule also extends Apple’s child safety push this year, which included a global rollout of its age assurance technology. Apple has since previewed new parental controls and child safety features .

The second descriptor, Shared Location, asks whether an app shares a user’s real-world location with another person or group. Apple said that declaration may not affect minimum ratings in some regions. Location sharing a user doesn’t know about is an obvious privacy risk, and the declaration puts that feature on the record.

Brazil is the exception Apple spelled out. Local rules there require an A16 rating for Shared Location and an A18 rating for Dating and Relationships. Parent-and-child family apps can skip the A16 default by requesting an official rating from Brazil’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP) . Once the ministry verifies it, Apple will show that rating on the Brazilian App Store.

The notice leaves open questions. How will Apple check that a developer’s answers match what the app actually does? What happens to an app that misses the deadline? And how will the new rating work alongside Apple’s age assurance tools on a teen’s device?

The new questions appear in App Store Connect on November 16. Developers must answer them when they submit an update or edit their age rating questionnaire. Every app needs both declarations filed by January 12, 2027, and any companion app that answers yes on romance gets the 18+ minimum.

sources.title: Google responds to political backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI - CNBC
passages: Google is playing defense on Tuesday after a political backlash to its new policy surrounding use of artificial intelligence in schools.
In a blog post titled "Designing responsible AI for learning," Google said it's bringing AI into its Classroom offering with a product called Guided Learning.
The New York Times published a story saying that the company will turn off search for schools that reject AI entirely.
Google said its Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook and search are turned off by default, and that "schools are in control," with the ability to turn them as they see fit.
The company's post didn't explicitly respond to the claim that access to search requires use of AI.
However, Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told the Times that "Search and AI are deeply integrated."
"Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don't get quick answers to schoolwork."
"Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools," Mamdani wrote on X.
Sanders wrote that "Google is threatening schools," referring to the policy as "extortion."
Google introduced AI overviews as a search function in May 2024 .
Google's broader practices have come under fire in recent years, with the company losing antitrust cases over its search and advertising businesses.
Former Federal Trade Commission Chair Lina Khan aggressively pursued Google and other tech giants, including Meta and Amazon .
A Google spokesperson referred CNBC to the X post when asked for comment.
The nonprofit Common Sense Media recently gave Google's AI overviews an " unacceptable risk " rating.
Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo., launched an inquiry over Google's push of AI into classrooms.
— CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos contributed to this report.

passages: The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search “will be entirely off” for K-12 student accounts unless “administrators explicitly turn them on.” Administrators will not be given the option to toggle Gemini-powered features off without disabling Search, however.
Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times.
Several lawmakers and local leaders have responded to Google’s move to block Search, with Sen.
The move added to skepticism surrounding Google’s introduction of AI in schools amid reports of declining test scores and other impacts on students’ learning abilities.

passages: Benton Institute for Broadband & Society 1041 Ridge Rd, Unit 214 Wilmette, IL 60091

Google announced that early in 2027 it would turn off artificial intelligence tools in its popular software for K-12 students, unless school administrators explicitly choose to make such tools available.
Executives at the tech giant said they wanted to be responsive to educators and parents who have asked for more control in how children interact with AI.
But there is a catch: Schools that choose to restrict AI entirely will also lose access to Google search.
AI features are now a standard part of Google’s commercially available search engine.
“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” said Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google.
If a school has banned AI, he added, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

But because search is integrated with AI, schools that opt out of AI altogether would also lose access to Google search."We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach," Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post.The company also said it is updating its search tools to make them "better for learning," including offering step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don't get quick answers to schoolwork."But turning off AI altogether is not possible if schools want to use Google products.Google is by far the dominant provider of education technology for U.S. schools. Worldwide, the company says 150 million students and teachers use its Google Classroom platform, and many students use school-provided Chromebook computers.Google faced an outcry in August when it switched on its Gemini chatbot for many K-12 students. Until August, Google had only allowed Gemini to be turned on for students 18 or older.Tuesday's announcement was met with swift criticism from educators and policymakers."Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI. "As the public increasingly pushes back against the use of AI in schools, Google is making clear it will punish those who don't fall in line."New York City and Los Angeles, home to the nation's biggest school districts, have issued temporary bans on generative AI tools in elementary and middle schools as they assess AI use and safety and develop policies on its use.Many students already use AI to help with school and homework, but the technology has also made it easier to cheat and find quick, easy answers to questions instead of thinking critically. And experts have raised questions about how access to AI is affecting children's brain development.Josh Golin, executive director of children's advocacy group Fairplay, said Google's attempt to "strong-arm schools into using its AI products is likely to backfire." He said Google's technology in schools is not about learning but about "developing lifetime brand loyalty" for its products."Because AI isn't safe for kids and undermines education and critical thinking, schools should turn off Google's AI tools the minute that option becomes available," Golin said in a statement.Rather than fret about losing access to search, Golin urged schools to turn off not just AI but also Google, and "use this opportunity to help students find more privacy-protective alternatives for search, as well as ways to do more substantive research beyond search and click."

coreStoryFacts.text: Google is playing defense on Tuesday after a political backlash to its new policy surrounding use of artificial intelligence in schools.
In a blog post titled "Designing responsible AI for learning," Google said it's bringing AI into its Classroom offering with a product called Guided Learning.
The New York Times published a story saying that the company will turn off search for schools that reject AI entirely.
Google said its Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook and search are turned off by default, and that "schools are in control," with the ability to turn them as they see fit.
The company's post didn't explicitly respond to the claim that access to search requires use of AI.
However, Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told the Times that "Search and AI are deeply integrated."
"Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don't get quick answers to schoolwork."
"Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools," Mamdani wrote on X.
Sanders wrote that "Google is threatening schools," referring to the policy as "extortion."
Google introduced AI overviews as a search function in May 2024 .
Google's broader practices have come under fire in recent years, with the company losing antitrust cases over its search and advertising businesses.
Former Federal Trade Commission Chair Lina Khan aggressively pursued Google and other tech giants, including Meta and Amazon .
A Google spokesperson referred CNBC to the X post when asked for comment.
The nonprofit Common Sense Media recently gave Google's AI overviews an " unacceptable risk " rating.
Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo., launched an inquiry over Google's push of AI into classrooms.
— CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos contributed to this report.

The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search “will be entirely off” for K-12 student accounts unless “administrators explicitly turn them on.” Administrators will not be given the option to toggle Gemini-powered features off without disabling Search, however.
Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times.
Several lawmakers and local leaders have responded to Google’s move to block Search, with Sen.
The move added to skepticism surrounding Google’s introduction of AI in schools amid reports of declining test scores and other impacts on students’ learning abilities.

Bernie Sanders (D-VT) calling it “extortion” and NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani saying, “no corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.” Rohit Chopra, California’s Secretary of Business & Consumer Services, wrote that Big Tech shouldn’t be able to “strong-arm schools.” Google argues that this change will “give schools more choice, not less,” adding that schools can choose to turn off each service on or off individually.
The announcement comes just months after Google turned its Gemini AI assistant on by default inside the Google Classroom app, which is used by more than 150 million teachers and students globally.
Google will begin testing this feature in select US schools this month.
Update, November 3rd: Added responses from lawmakers and Google.

passages: Benton Institute for Broadband & Society 1041 Ridge Rd, Unit 214 Wilmette, IL 60091

Google announced that early in 2027 it would turn off artificial intelligence tools in its popular software for K-12 students, unless school administrators explicitly choose to make such tools available.
Executives at the tech giant said they wanted to be responsive to educators and parents who have asked for more control in how children interact with AI.
But there is a catch: Schools that choose to restrict AI entirely will also lose access to Google search.
AI features are now a standard part of Google’s commercially available search engine.
“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” said Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google.
If a school has banned AI, he added, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

sources.title: Valve is making changes to deal with a ‘significant increase’ in Steam game submissions
passages: In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days.

Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.” The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes.

“This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.” Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install.
Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates.
Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

Steam users are calling for Valve to change its current regional pricing system after "unfair" differences came to light – some that see local prices that are up to 20% or 30% higher than their United States dollar equivalents. YouTuber Water CS2 points out these differences in a new video , aptly dubbed "Steam has a pricing problem." He uses the recent Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater as an example of the disparity, which he points out is "priced at $69.99 USD in the States." However, players in other regions, like Poland, are paying much more. "You would assume a fair price, roughly the equivalent of the dollar price," says Water CS2, "but instead it's 369.99 PLN." Using Google's exchange rate "of approximately 3.66 PLN to $1 USD," he determines that the game costs over $101 in Poland when its price is converted to US dollars. "That makes the game roughly $31 more expensive than in the US," describes the YouTuber. "A whopping 30% increase. A Polish gamer is paying more than someone living in New York for the exact same digital file." This "significant price disparity for PC games" doesn't seem fair. As Water CS2 points out, this issue isn't exclusive to just Metal Gear. "Local prices are often 20% to 30% higher than the dollar equivalent," he details, and it all boils down to Steam's regional pricing system. "The idea is great. Games shouldn't cost the same everywhere because $60 means something very different in the US than it does in Brazil. Valve uses complex economics like purchasing power parity to suggest lower prices in regions with less buying power." In theory, this should make games "more accessible to a larger audience." But, as Water CS2 says, "The problem lies in the data Valve uses to make these suggestions." According to the YouTuber, Valve hasn't updated its conversion rates since 2022, when it first introduced the regional pricing system. At that point in time, "the Polish currency was near its weakest" – but Steam is still "using this weak old rate" from three years ago. "The regional pricing system was meant to make games affordable, not expensive," Water CS2 concludes. This, unfortunately, doesn't seem to reflect the reality of how it's played out without any adjustments, though. "It is now a direct cause of the unfair prices Valve wanted to prevent in the first place. Valve must stop making excuses and fix its core pricing data immediately." The comments show users affected by said unfair prices agreeing. "As a Polish man, thank you for covering this issue," reads one. "I'm a teen who doesn't have a lot of money, and it would be nice if the games were a bit cheaper for us." Another chimes in, "Thank you for covering this issue. We have been trying to reach English-speaking press and YouTubers to no avail." One adds, "Thanks for making a video on this, I'm tired of paying 20% more on everything just because of my currency on Steam." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Here's hoping Valve hears the community's complaints now and tweaks the regional pricing system to better reflect the current conversion rate, making things a bit fairer for all Steam users – regardless of their location. sources.title: Valve changes Steam's pre-release review process - Oyun Günlüğü
passages: Valve has made changes to the pre-release review process that games go through before launching on Steam.
According to information Oyun Günlüğü obtained from Steamworks, build reviews that typically take 3-5 days are currently taking up to 12 business days.
Valve explained that much of this delay comes from games having to be re-reviewed, and the new changes are designed to prevent that.

Citing a significant increase in store page and build review submissions in recent months, the company has added new items to the release checklist to help more developers pass review on the first try and reduce re-reviews caused by basic functional issues.
Valve noted that it sometimes receives builds that have never been played through Steam.
Developers now need to launch their game with the green “Play” button in Steam and run it for at least 5 minutes before submitting it for review.
Playtime from any user counts, but it must be within the past 7 days, or since the last build if it was uploaded more than 7 days ago.
This ensures launch options are configured correctly and the necessary content depots are included.

Valve reminded developers that its review team mainly checks whether the store page is clear and complete, whether the game matches what the store page promises, and whether sensitive content such as AI usage and mature content is properly disclosed in the content survey.

For example, games promising multiple languages are asked to confirm those languages are included in the build, while games with online multiplayer need to make sure servers are available for testing and provide any special credentials the review team needs.
Developers must also specify which common redistributables Steam should install, such as DirectX, Visual C++, .NET and XNA, or confirm that their game doesn’t need any.
New checks also flag incomplete achievement setups, including missing names, missing icons and duplicate names.

For games that support Steam Cloud, a member of the developer’s partner group must write a save file to Steam Cloud to confirm the save path is set up properly, and the system will warn developers if developer mode is still enabled for cloud sync.

relevantPassages.text: Valve has made changes to the pre-release review process that games go through before launching on Steam.
According to information Oyun Günlüğü obtained from Steamworks, build reviews that typically take 3-5 days are currently taking up to 12 business days.
Valve explained that much of this delay comes from games having to be re-reviewed, and the new changes are designed to prevent that.

Citing a significant increase in store page and build review submissions in recent months, the company has added new items to the release checklist to help more developers pass review on the first try and reduce re-reviews caused by basic functional issues.
Valve noted that it sometimes receives builds that have never been played through Steam.
Developers now need to launch their game with the green “Play” button in Steam and run it for at least 5 minutes before submitting it for review.
Playtime from any user counts, but it must be within the past 7 days, or since the last build if it was uploaded more than 7 days ago.
This ensures launch options are configured correctly and the necessary content depots are included.

Valve reminded developers that its review team mainly checks whether the store page is clear and complete, whether the game matches what the store page promises, and whether sensitive content such as AI usage and mature content is properly disclosed in the content survey.

For example, games promising multiple languages are asked to confirm those languages are included in the build, while games with online multiplayer need to make sure servers are available for testing and provide any special credentials the review team needs.
Developers must also specify which common redistributables Steam should install, such as DirectX, Visual C++, .NET and XNA, or confirm that their game doesn’t need any.
New checks also flag incomplete achievement setups, including missing names, missing icons and duplicate names.

For games that support Steam Cloud, a member of the developer’s partner group must write a save file to Steam Cloud to confirm the save path is set up properly, and the system will warn developers if developer mode is still enabled for cloud sync.

passages: Valve says Steam reviews are taking up to 12 business days after indie games missing launch dates prompted developers to describe weeks-long delays.
The company acknowledged a significant increase in submissions for store and page reviews in recent months and said it is running behind.
Kamon and publisher 2 Left Thumbs suspect a flood of low-quality AI-generated games may be contributing to the delays.

Kamon said: “We can only assume it’s because Steam’s review queue is clogged up by AI slop, but the whole process is now taking several weeks for some developers.” That is their explanation, not a cause Valve has confirmed.
The company said some of the delay comes from having to review games again.
The scale of submissions has risen alongside Steam’s game events.
October’s Steam Next Fest featured 7,240 games, 65.2 percent more than the June event, according to figures cited in the source material.
A Reddit user also found that 49.9 percent of games released since Valve began asking developers in 2024 to label titles using AI had an AI disclosure.
For small studios, a missed date can unsettle a carefully planned release.
Developers say they have been left waiting without knowing when Steam will approve their games.
Valve has also updated its release checklist, requiring developers to run a game through Steam for at least five minutes.
It says further improvements to the build review process are on the way.
Game director Alfred Kamon said Studio Daimon had sent another support ticket the previous week to flag the urgency, but had received no response.
The English-language global edition of JournalArta.
Valve’s standard guidance says a review of a game’s store presence typically takes 3-5 business days.

Valve says Steam reviews are taking up to 12 business days after indie games missing launch dates prompted developers to describe weeks-long delays. The company acknowledged a significant increase in submissions for store and page reviews in recent months and said it is running behind.

The backlog has already disrupted release plans. Studio Daimon expected to launch Food Devils in early access on November 4, but the game was still awaiting approval after the team submitted its build on October 12.
For small studios, a missed date can unsettle a carefully planned release. Developers say they have been left waiting without knowing when Steam will approve their games.
Steam’s review queue has grown as submissions increased, according to Valve. The company said some of the delay comes from having to review games again.

Game director Alfred Kamon said Studio Daimon had sent another support ticket the previous week to flag the urgency, but had received no response. “Even now, we don’t know when Steam will give us the final OK to finally release our game,” he wrote.

Kamon and publisher 2 Left Thumbs suspect a flood of low-quality AI-generated games may be contributing to the delays. Kamon said: “We can only assume it’s because Steam’s review queue is clogged up by AI slop, but the whole process is now taking several weeks for some developers.” That is their explanation, not a cause Valve has confirmed.

Valve’s standard guidance says a review of a game’s store presence typically takes 3-5 business days. It advises developers to submit a page at least 7 business days before they want it to go live, allowing time for changes.

The company’s newer update gives a different picture of current waits: reviews are now taking up to 12 business days. Valve has also updated its release checklist, requiring developers to run a game through Steam for at least five minutes. It says further improvements to the build review process are on the way.

The delay has affected more than one release. In October, publisher 2 Left Thumbs said it missed its planned launch of Wheel Make It by nearly two weeks because of long build-review waits. The publisher also described failing a review over a single menu option that could not be accessed with a controller.

The scale of submissions has risen alongside Steam’s game events. October’s Steam Next Fest featured 7,240 games, 65.2 percent more than the June event, according to figures cited in the source material. A Reddit user also found that 49.9 percent of games released since Valve began asking developers in 2024 to label titles using AI had an AI disclosure.

Itch.io has reported growth too. The platform said the number of game pages created each day had doubled in the past 2 months. The volume puts the review bottleneck in context, while leaving developers facing the immediate problem: release plans depend on approval they cannot schedule with confidence.
Valve’s current estimate is up to 12 business days for reviews.
The English-language global edition of JournalArta.

coreStoryFacts.text: In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days.

Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.” The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes.

“This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.” Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install.
Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates.
Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

Steam users are calling for Valve to change its current regional pricing system after "unfair" differences came to light – some that see local prices that are up to 20% or 30% higher than their United States dollar equivalents.
As Water CS2 points out, this issue isn't exclusive to just Metal Gear.
Games shouldn't cost the same everywhere because $60 means something very different in the US than it does in Brazil.
Valve uses complex economics like purchasing power parity to suggest lower prices in regions with less buying power."
This, unfortunately, doesn't seem to reflect the reality of how it's played out without any adjustments, though.
"It is now a direct cause of the unfair prices Valve wanted to prevent in the first place.
Valve must stop making excuses and fix its core pricing data immediately." The comments show users affected by said unfair prices agreeing.
At that point in time, "the Polish currency was near its weakest" – but Steam is still "using this weak old rate" from three years ago.
"You would assume a fair price, roughly the equivalent of the dollar price," says Water CS2, "but instead it's 369.99 PLN."
Using Google's exchange rate "of approximately 3.66 PLN to $1 USD," he determines that the game costs over $101 in Poland when its price is converted to US dollars.
"As a Polish man, thank you for covering this issue," reads one.

We have been trying to reach English-speaking press and YouTubers to no avail." One adds, "Thanks for making a video on this, I'm tired of paying 20% more on everything just because of my currency on Steam."
"For the first time ever," Valve reminds us, the Steam Autumn Sale is live 2 months early – like, right now

Steam users are calling for Valve to change its current regional pricing system after "unfair" differences came to light – some that see local prices that are up to 20% or 30% higher than their United States dollar equivalents. YouTuber Water CS2 points out these differences in a new video , aptly dubbed "Steam has a pricing problem." He uses the recent Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater as an example of the disparity, which he points out is "priced at $69.99 USD in the States." However, players in other regions, like Poland, are paying much more. "You would assume a fair price, roughly the equivalent of the dollar price," says Water CS2, "but instead it's 369.99 PLN." Using Google's exchange rate "of approximately 3.66 PLN to $1 USD," he determines that the game costs over $101 in Poland when its price is converted to US dollars. "That makes the game roughly $31 more expensive than in the US," describes the YouTuber. "A whopping 30% increase. A Polish gamer is paying more than someone living in New York for the exact same digital file." This "significant price disparity for PC games" doesn't seem fair. As Water CS2 points out, this issue isn't exclusive to just Metal Gear. "Local prices are often 20% to 30% higher than the dollar equivalent," he details, and it all boils down to Steam's regional pricing system. "The idea is great. Games shouldn't cost the same everywhere because $60 means something very different in the US than it does in Brazil. Valve uses complex economics like purchasing power parity to suggest lower prices in regions with less buying power." In theory, this should make games "more accessible to a larger audience." But, as Water CS2 says, "The problem lies in the data Valve uses to make these suggestions." According to the YouTuber, Valve hasn't updated its conversion rates since 2022, when it first introduced the regional pricing system. At that point in time, "the Polish currency was near its weakest" – but Steam is still "using this weak old rate" from three years ago. "The regional pricing system was meant to make games affordable, not expensive," Water CS2 concludes. This, unfortunately, doesn't seem to reflect the reality of how it's played out without any adjustments, though. "It is now a direct cause of the unfair prices Valve wanted to prevent in the first place. Valve must stop making excuses and fix its core pricing data immediately." The comments show users affected by said unfair prices agreeing. "As a Polish man, thank you for covering this issue," reads one. "I'm a teen who doesn't have a lot of money, and it would be nice if the games were a bit cheaper for us." Another chimes in, "Thank you for covering this issue. We have been trying to reach English-speaking press and YouTubers to no avail." One adds, "Thanks for making a video on this, I'm tired of paying 20% more on everything just because of my currency on Steam." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Here's hoping Valve hears the community's complaints now and tweaks the regional pricing system to better reflect the current conversion rate, making things a bit fairer for all Steam users – regardless of their location. passages: Valve has made changes to the pre-release review process that games go through before launching on Steam.
According to information Oyun Günlüğü obtained from Steamworks, build reviews that typically take 3-5 days are currently taking up to 12 business days.
Valve explained that much of this delay comes from games having to be re-reviewed, and the new changes are designed to prevent that.

Citing a significant increase in store page and build review submissions in recent months, the company has added new items to the release checklist to help more developers pass review on the first try and reduce re-reviews caused by basic functional issues.
Valve noted that it sometimes receives builds that have never been played through Steam.

This ensures launch options are configured correctly and the necessary content depots are included.

Valve reminded developers that its review team mainly checks whether the store page is clear and complete, whether the game matches what the store page promises, and whether sensitive content such as AI usage and mature content is properly disclosed in the content survey.

For example, games promising multiple languages are asked to confirm those languages are included in the build, while games with online multiplayer need to make sure servers are available for testing and provide any special credentials the review team needs.

New checks also flag incomplete achievement setups, including missing names, missing icons and duplicate names.

sources.title: Indie games missing launch dates as Steam review queue grows - JournalArta
passages: Valve says Steam reviews are taking up to 12 business days after indie games missing launch dates prompted developers to describe weeks-long delays.
The company acknowledged a significant increase in submissions for store and page reviews in recent months and said it is running behind.
Kamon and publisher 2 Left Thumbs suspect a flood of low-quality AI-generated games may be contributing to the delays.

Kamon said: “We can only assume it’s because Steam’s review queue is clogged up by AI slop, but the whole process is now taking several weeks for some developers.” That is their explanation, not a cause Valve has confirmed.
The company said some of the delay comes from having to review games again.
The scale of submissions has risen alongside Steam’s game events.
October’s Steam Next Fest featured 7,240 games, 65.2 percent more than the June event, according to figures cited in the source material.
A Reddit user also found that 49.9 percent of games released since Valve began asking developers in 2024 to label titles using AI had an AI disclosure.
For small studios, a missed date can unsettle a carefully planned release.
Developers say they have been left waiting without knowing when Steam will approve their games.
Valve has also updated its release checklist, requiring developers to run a game through Steam for at least five minutes.
It says further improvements to the build review process are on the way.
Game director Alfred Kamon said Studio Daimon had sent another support ticket the previous week to flag the urgency, but had received no response.
The English-language global edition of JournalArta.
Valve’s standard guidance says a review of a game’s store presence typically takes 3-5 business days.

extraction.body: MEPs agree to implement deal almost 12 months after it was proposed and just days before deadline of US threat to raise tariffs MEPs agree to implement deal almost 12 months after it was proposed and just days before deadline of US threat to raise tariffs The European parliament has given its final approval to implement last July’s tariff agreement with Donald Trump . Facing a threat of increased tariffs if the deal was not sanctioned by 4 July, MEPs agreed to approve the deal, with two main provisos. The first is a “sunset clause” which will mean the deal expires on 31 December 2029 unless it is renewed. The second sets out “clear conditions” for tariff reductions on products containing some steel and aluminium, tariffs that Trump has imposed under national security laws rather than the tariff regime he instituted on “liberation day” last April. Under the deal the US applies 15% on most EU exports, while the EU has cut import duties on some US goods, some agricultural products and a wide range of seafood to 0%. The deal is expected to be formally adopted by EU leaders when they meet in Brussels on Thursday. The European parliament’s approval came nearly a year after the original deal was agreed at Donald Trump’s Turnberry golf course in Scotland last July, having gone through a democratic process that has baffled the US administration, which put the deal in place stateside immediately last summer. However, relations with the EU soured when the US, under the guise of national security considerations, imposed tariffs on products with steel or aluminium content, something Brussels has frequently protested against. Under the text of the agreement voted on in the European parliament on Tuesday, the European Commission will be able to suspend tariff preferences for US goods by 31 December 2026 if the US continues to apply tariffs on steel derivatives. The commission will report to the parliament on the matter by 1 December. By 30 June 2029, six months after Trump’s presidency is due to end, the commission is now also required by the parliament to conduct an assessment of the impact on EU industry of the 0% tariffs on US goods for agriculture and small- to medium-sized businesses. MEPs suspended the ratification process twice this year through the international trade committee, first in protest against Trump’s threat to impose higher tariffs in January, and then over his threat take over Greenland. Although the supreme court in the US has already ruled the 15% tariff at the heart of the deal is illegal , the EU agreed to maintain the agreement in an attempt to achieve stability for businesses and industry.

extraction.body: COPENHAGEN, Nov 3 (Reuters) – Greenland’s parliament on Tuesday ratified the Arctic island’s security agreement struck earlier this year with US President Donald Trump, although some opposition party members questioned the deal’s economic value. The United States, Denmark and Greenland in September signed the agreement, aimed at ending tensions after Trump’s repeated threats to take control of the strategically located and mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory. The deal expands the US military’s role in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and Trump’s “Golden Dome” missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. A majority of lawmakers had already signalled support for the deal in a first debate last month. Tuesday’s vote was 16 in favour and none against, with 7 abstentions. The White House in January said Trump was discussing options for acquiring Greenland, including potential use of the US military, alarming governments in Europe and triggering intense diplomatic efforts to calm the situation. Greenlandic Foreign Minister Mute Egede said on Tuesday that ratification of the deal was an important step for the island. “We must accept that peace and stability are no longer something we can take for granted,” Egede told lawmakers in Nuuk shortly before the vote. Opposition party Naleraq, the most prominent political voice for Greenland’s independence, questioned the deal’s economic value during the debate. “We are looking for a better agreement that we can benefit from when we become an independent state. But no economic benefit has been gained from the agreement,” Naleraq chair Pele Broberg said. The Danish parliament is due to give the bill a first reading on November 11, followed by a second reading and a vote on November 19. The executive agreement will enter into force once Denmark and Greenland have ratified it, and does not require approval from the US Senate. sources.title: Greenland's parliament ratifies Trump's trilateral security agreement, expanding US military presence - DW.com
passages: Greenland's parliament on Tuesday signed off on a trilateral security and military-access agreement with the United States and Denmark that paves the way for an expanded US' military presence on the strategically located and mineral-rich island.
The agreement allows for two new US military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system.
It also keeps Greenland under Danish control, while reaffirming Greenlanders' right to self determination.
In January 2026, Trump began calling for the US to control Greenland, and threatened the use of military force and tariffs against US European allies if he did not get his way.
Under a 1951 agreement, the US already has considerable military freedom of action in Greenland.
After years of voluntarily drawing down its military presence, the US only maintains the Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland, which is used for missile defense and radar surveillance.

After months of negotiation the agreement was signed in September by Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.
Critics have pointed out the same deal could have been made without the extreme disruption caused by Trump's territorial and tariff threats.
Pele Broberg, chair of the pro-independence Naleraq party, questioned the deal's value for Greenland.
The agreement will come into effect after ratification by the Danish parliament, which is due to read the bill over two sessions in November.
Trump had claimed that Denmark was not doing enough to defend its autonomous arctic territory from unspecified threats from China and Russia.

extraction.body: COPENHAGEN, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Greenland's parliament on Tuesday ratified the Arctic island's security agreement struck earlier this year with US President Donald Trump, although some opposition party members questioned the deal's economic value. The United States, Denmark and Greenland in September signed the agreement, aimed at ending tensions after Trump's repeated threats to take control of the strategically located and mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory. The deal expands the US military's role in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination. A majority of lawmakers had already signalled support for the deal in a first debate last month. Tuesday's vote was 16 in favour and none against, with 7 abstentions. The White House in January said Trump was discussing options for acquiring Greenland, including potential use of the US military, alarming governments in Europe and triggering intense diplomatic efforts to calm the situation. Greenlandic Foreign Minister Mute Egede said on Tuesday that ratification of the deal was an important step for the island. "We must accept that peace and stability are no longer something we can take for granted," Egede told lawmakers in Nuuk shortly before the vote. Opposition party Naleraq, the most prominent political voice for Greenland's independence, questioned the deal's economic value during the debate. "We are looking for a better agreement that we can benefit from when we become an independent state. But no economic benefit has been gained from the agreement," Naleraq chair Pele Broberg said. The Danish parliament is due to give the bill a first reading on November 11, followed by a second reading and a vote on November 19. The executive agreement will enter into force once Denmark and Greenland have ratified it, and does not require approval from the US Senate. (Reporting by Louise Rasmussen and Stine Jacobsen, editing by Terje Solsvik and Gareth Jones)

extraction.body: MEPs agree to implement deal almost 12 months after it was proposed and just days before deadline of US threat to raise tariffs MEPs agree to implement deal almost 12 months after it was proposed and just days before deadline of US threat to raise tariffs The European parliament has given its final approval to implement last July’s tariff agreement with Donald Trump . Facing a threat of increased tariffs if the deal was not sanctioned by 4 July, MEPs agreed to approve the deal, with two main provisos. The first is a “sunset clause” which will mean the deal expires on 31 December 2029 unless it is renewed. The second sets out “clear conditions” for tariff reductions on products containing some steel and aluminium, tariffs that Trump has imposed under national security laws rather than the tariff regime he instituted on “liberation day” last April. Under the deal the US applies 15% on most EU exports, while the EU has cut import duties on some US goods, some agricultural products and a wide range of seafood to 0%. The deal is expected to be formally adopted by EU leaders when they meet in Brussels on Thursday. The European parliament’s approval came nearly a year after the original deal was agreed at Donald Trump’s Turnberry golf course in Scotland last July, having gone through a democratic process that has baffled the US administration, which put the deal in place stateside immediately last summer. However, relations with the EU soured when the US, under the guise of national security considerations, imposed tariffs on products with steel or aluminium content, something Brussels has frequently protested against. Under the text of the agreement voted on in the European parliament on Tuesday, the European Commission will be able to suspend tariff preferences for US goods by 31 December 2026 if the US continues to apply tariffs on steel derivatives. The commission will report to the parliament on the matter by 1 December. By 30 June 2029, six months after Trump’s presidency is due to end, the commission is now also required by the parliament to conduct an assessment of the impact on EU industry of the 0% tariffs on US goods for agriculture and small- to medium-sized businesses. MEPs suspended the ratification process twice this year through the international trade committee, first in protest against Trump’s threat to impose higher tariffs in January, and then over his threat take over Greenland. Although the supreme court in the US has already ruled the 15% tariff at the heart of the deal is illegal , the EU agreed to maintain the agreement in an attempt to achieve stability for businesses and industry.

sources.title: Greenland parliament ratifies security deal reached with Trump - ThePrint
passages: COPENHAGEN, Nov 3 (Reuters) – Greenland’s parliament on Tuesday ratified the Arctic island’s security agreement struck earlier this year with US President Donald Trump, although some opposition party members questioned the deal’s economic value.

The deal expands the US military’s role in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and Trump’s “Golden Dome” missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.

The United States, Denmark and Greenland in September signed the agreement, aimed at ending tensions after Trump’s repeated threats to take control of the strategically located and mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory.
